name: Freelance bug-hunting tester (Test IO)
summary: Free crowdtesting platform that pays testers per accepted bug or test for exploratory testing of apps and websites.
whatYouDo: You join test cycles, explore a client's app or website, and report bugs with clear reproduction steps; team leads review and accept or reject them. Pay is per accepted bug or completed test.
appeal: Free to register; official scam warning says testers never pay to join
Beginners praise the onboarding and training
Monthly payment to a bank account or PayPal
Good way to learn exploratory testing
watchOuts: Paid only for accepted bugs; reviewers describe inconsistent or biased team-lead decisions
Low-tier testers report few paid cases and low earnings for the hours spent
Canada not named explicitly; the community claims testers in 190+ countries and some tests are country-restricted

training.notes: Tester Academy materials; reviewers describe onboarding as useful.

compensation.notes: Official tester page: most valuable bugs pay up to $50; some special tests pay more (a community listing mentions up to $200). Paid monthly.

reliability.notes: G2/Trustpilot reviewers say basic-level testers get few cases; Trustpilot averages about 3.5/5 over ~200 reviews. Anecdotal.

applicationSteps: Register free as a tester on Test IO
Add a bank account or PayPal for monthly payment
Join available test cycles and submit bug reports
fitsIf: You enjoy hunting for bugs, write clear reports, and see it as paid practice for a QA career.
notFitIf: You dislike having work rejected without pay or need steady earnings.

sources.title: Become a Tester
sources.notes: No fee to register; bank account or PayPal; monthly payment; bugs up to $50; contact testersupport@test.io. Direct fetch blocked.

sources.title: Test IO Community - Join Global Testing Professionals

sources.title: Test IO reviews
sources.notes: About 3.5/5 over ~200 reviews; complaints about biased/rude team leads; praise for training. Anecdotal.

sources.title: Test IO Reviews
sources.notes: Reviewer: hard to earn as a basic-badge tester due to few cases.
